title: lib/config validates keys but not values, so a boolean key holding any word but true/yes/1 or false/no/0 is silently misread
body:
## Summary

**`lib/config` checks that a key is one devbin knows, never that its value is one devbin reads. So a boolean key holding any other word is silently read the wrong way.**

Every boolean key reads its value through `is_true_word` or `is_false_word` (lib/helpers, issue 0066). Those take `true`/`yes`/`1` and `false`/`no`/`0` exactly, and nothing else. Nothing refuses any other value:

- `commands.<cmd>.enabled: off` is neither a false word nor a true word. A built-in command stays active, and an opt-in command stays off. Nothing is printed either way.
- `commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>.in_all: off` leaves the option in `all`.
- `options.<name>.flag: on` leaves the option valued, and `--name` then demands a value.
- The same goes for `True`, `YES`, `enable`, and any typo.

## Why it matters

These are the keys that decide what runs. A project that writes `enabled: off` has said what it means, and devbin does the opposite without a word. The failure is quiet in exactly the way the true/false predicates were built to prevent: the vocabulary is now one place, but nothing tells a project it has left it.

## Found

2026-09-16, by critic-shell reviewing 0066. vc agreed it is its own issue.

## The shape of a fix

- In the validator, for each key devbin reads as a boolean, refuse a value that is neither `is_true_word` nor `is_false_word`.
- The refusal names the key, the value, and the accepted words, read from `_DEVBIN_TRUE_WORDS` and `_DEVBIN_FALSE_WORDS` so the message cannot drift from the predicates.
- The list of boolean keys should live in one place that the readers and the validator share, or the validator becomes a second copy of the key set.

## Arms a fix needs

- `enabled: off` on a built-in, and on an opt-in, is refused by name.
- Each accepted word still validates.
- A mutation that drops one boolean key from the validator goes red.

## Fixed 2026-09-17 -- doctor refuses a boolean key holding any other word, from one list of those keys (vc), reviewed by dc

**Commits:**
- `1da7bcd`: the validator, the list, doctor's heading and the docs.
- `a741272`: dc's review fold. The docs had claimed a refusal that only `doctor` makes, and the release note was missing.

**The list.** `_cfg_path_boolean` in `lib/config` is the one statement of the keys devbin reads as a yes or a no: `commands.<cmd>.enabled`, `commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>.enabled` and `.in_all`, and `options.<name>.flag`. `cfg_validate` refuses any other value on those keys. It names the key and the value, and lists the accepted words, read from `_DEVBIN_TRUE_WORDS` and `_DEVBIN_FALSE_WORDS`, so the message cannot drift from the predicates. `log:` and `options.<name>.value` stay free, because they take other words. `cfg_validate` refuses to run without `lib/helpers` rather than report every boolean value as wrong. `doctor`'s heading now says `keys or values the schema does not know`.

**What holds it:**
- `enabled: off` is refused on a built-in and on an opt-in, naming the key, the value and both word lists.
- Every boolean key refuses `off`, `on`, `True`, `YES`, `enable` and an empty value, and accepts all six words.
- CONTROL arms: `log: MYSUFFIX` at command and option level, and `options.<name>.value: compact`, both validate.
- Every `is_true_word` or `is_false_word "$(cfg_get "<path>"` reader in `lib/` and `bin/devbin` must be a path `_cfg_path_boolean` accepts. The extractor is guarded at 4 or more, and finds 4.
- `docs/configuration.md` names exactly the six words, in list order.
- `doctor` fails on `enabled: off`, naming the value.

**Mutations killed.** vc: drop `in_all`; drop `options.flag`; widen to command-level `log`; widen to `options.<name>.value`; drop the helpers guard; check only the true words; a doc word changed; a seventh word added to the list. dc: drop command-level `enabled`; drop option-level `enabled`; omit the value from the refusal; accept case-insensitively. dc's D4 (drop the `options` segment test) survived and is equivalent, because `_cfg_path_known` admits no other 5-segment `commands` path.

**Suite:** 1223/1223 at `1da7bcd`, rc 0, 3 standing skips. dc re-ran the arms in its own worktree and scanned 14 estate configs read-only: none holds a non-word on these keys, so a sweep turns no estate's doctor red.

**Residuals, declared.**
- Only `doctor` validates, as for unknown keys: the command you run still reads `enabled: off` without a word. Validating at dispatch would change behaviour across the fleet, and that is hv's call. It is not filed.
- The reader-extraction arm sees only the `is_X_word "$(cfg_get "<path>"` shape. A reader that stores the value in a variable first would escape it, and today there is none.
